entry.title: Revocation must reach every live stream
entry.summary: ntfy removed a user's access or account, but its teardown helper stopped after cancelling the first matching subscription. Other live streams could continue receiving that topic's messages until they disconnected.

entry.title: A role name is not an SQL fragment
entry.summary: Navidrome treated an artist role as a small, enum-like value but inserted the raw request string into an SQL ORDER BY expression. Any authenticated web user could cross that syntax boundary and execute arbitrary SQL against the application database.

entry.title: A share owner is not request data
entry.summary: Navidrome let a logged-in user assign a new share to someone with broader library access by submitting that user's ID. On affected multi-library installations, the share could expose tracks its creator was not allowed to read or stream.

entry.title: A valid signature is not a valid login
entry.summary: authentik verified a SAML assertion's signature and lifetime without proving it was meant for that SAML Source or tied to its login request. Because accepted assertions were not remembered, a valid assertion could also be replayed.

entry.title: Viewing is not revealing
entry.summary: authentik returned stored credentials when an account could view the configuration that contained them. Read-only access could therefore expose secrets used by connected systems.

entry.title: A guest memory limit does not cover host buffers
entry.summary: SurrealDB limited a module’s guest memory but buffered its unfinished output in unbounded host memory. A module could therefore exhaust the database process outside its configured ceiling.

entry.title: Not every header is text
entry.summary: SurrealDB's embedded JavaScript asserted that HTTP header bytes were text. A non-ASCII value could abort the server; version 3.3.0 made conversion total and non-panicking.

entry.title: OAuth is not a cookie-forwarding policy
entry.summary: Open WebUI’s OAuth-mode connectors forwarded each requesting user’s browser cookies to downstream servers. A destination could replay the leaked session cookie and impersonate that user.

entry.title: Export is not just another read
entry.summary: Open WebUI hid Python source from read-only tool users, but bulk export returned every readable tool with its source. Version 0.11.4 aligned export with write permission.

entry.title: An address range needs one total order
entry.summary: coturn compared IPv6 range endpoints byte by byte instead of as one ordered address. Under custom non-prefix-aligned deny rules, an authenticated client could relay traffic to peers the operator intended to block.

entry.title: Permissions do not bound state
entry.summary: coturn limited TURN permissions per IP, but multiplex-peer mode stored one shared demux entry per IP:port without a matching bound. Version 4.16.0 capped that state and made cleanup local to each allocation.

entry.title: A group ID does not carry its tenant
entry.summary: Vaultwarden accepted group IDs without proving they belonged to the current organization, then trusted a join missing the same tenant boundary. Together, the gaps granted cross-organization access to specific ciphers.

entry.title: Some URLs never need DNS
entry.summary: Vaultwarden checked the first icon host and DNS answers, but not IP-literal favicon URLs discovered in HTML. An unauthenticated request could therefore reach internal addresses.

entry.title: A length field is not an allocation budget
entry.summary: MediaMTX trusted compact MoQ length fields as slice sizes before checking whether the message could contain that much data. A small unauthenticated input could trigger an unrecoverable allocation panic and stop the entire media server.

entry.title: Panic recovery stays local
entry.summary: PocketBase recovered panics during ordinary request handling, but work moved into child goroutines lived beyond that boundary. A reachable panic could terminate the server instead of becoming a regular error.

entry.title: When identity data becomes policy syntax
entry.summary: Moquette inserted client IDs and usernames directly into pattern-based ACL rules. MQTT wildcard characters in those identities could broaden a tenant-scoped rule and grant cross-tenant read or write access.
